The '''2012 UEFA Champions League final''' was an [[association football]] match which took place on Saturday, 19 May 2012 between [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]] of Germany and [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] of England at the [[Allianz Arena]] in [[Munich]], Germany. The match was to decide the winner of the [[2011–12 UEFA Champions League|2011–12 season]] of the [[UEFA Champions League]], Europe's premier club football tournament. Bayern were making their ninth appearance in the competition's final, having won four and lost four, most recently losing in [[2010 UEFA Champions League final|2010]]. Chelsea were appearing in their second final, having lost their first in [[2008 UEFA Champions League final|2008]].

It was the first Champions League final to be held at the Allianz Arena (known as Fußball Arena München for the final). As tenants of the Arena, this meant Bayern were the first finalists to have home advantage since [[1984 European Cup final|1984]]. Both teams progressed to the knockout stages by finishing top of their group. Bayern then beat [[FC Basel|Basel]], [[Olympique de Marseille|Marseille]] and [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] to reach the final, while Chelsea knocked out [[SSC Napoli|Napoli]], [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]] and defending champions [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]].

Bayern took the lead late in the second half through [[Thomas Müller]],<ref name=ind13>{{cite web |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/people/profiles/thomas-muller-bayern-munich-couldnt-handle-losing-a-champions-league-final-again-8630153.html |title=Thomas Muller: Bayern Munich couldn't handle losing a Champions League final again |work=[[The Independent]] |author=Tim Rich |date=24 May 2013|access-date=19 December 2018|archive-date=4 April 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190404171713/https://www.independent.co.uk/news/people/profiles/thomas-muller-bayern-munich-couldnt-handle-losing-a-champions-league-final-again-8630153.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> but [[Didier Drogba]] equalised for Chelsea five minutes later to take the game to extra time, in which [[Arjen Robben]] missed an awarded penalty, [[Petr Čech]] saving the low drive. The teams stayed level at 1–1 and the match went to a [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shoot-out]], which Chelsea won 4–3 to clinch their first Champions League title.<ref name=guard12/> In doing so, they became the first London club to win the tournament, the fifth English club and 22nd overall.
[[File:Chelsea_Champions_League_trophy_parade_2012.jpg|thumb|259x259px|Chelsea held a triumphant open-top bus parade through west London on May 20, 2012, celebrating their 4-3 penalty win over Bayern Munich.]]
As winners, Chelsea took part in the [[2012 UEFA Super Cup]], losing 4–1 to [[Atlético Madrid]], the winners of the [[2011–12 UEFA Europa League]]. The victory also allowed them to enter the [[2012–13 UEFA Champions League|following season's Champions League competition]] (having failed to qualify for it by their league finishing position) at the expense of [[Chelsea F.C.–Tottenham Hotspur F.C. rivalry|London rivals]] [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]], who would otherwise have entered the competition having finished fourth in the [[Premier League]]. Chelsea also represented [[UEFA]] at the [[2012 FIFA Club World Cup]], entering at the semi-final stage; however, they were beaten 1–0 by [[Sport Club Corinthians Paulista|Corinthians]] in the [[2012 FIFA Club World Cup Final|final]].

==Venue==
[[File:Allianz Arena 2012 Champions League Final.jpg|thumb|left|The Allianz Arena in Champions League final livery]]

The [[Allianz Arena]] was announced by UEFA as the venue of the 2012 final on 30 January 2010, although the stadium was referred to as "Fußball Arena München" for the match, as UEFA does not recognise sponsorship by companies that are not among its partner organisations.<ref>{{cite news |title=UEFA unveil 2011 and 2012 final venues |url=https://www.uefa.com/news-media/news/01d5-0e70c9e763c9-0b023fd4e3e9-1000--uefa-unveil-2011-and-2012-final-venues/ |work=[[UEFA]] |publisher=Union of European Football Associations |date=30 January 2009 |access-date=24 March 2010 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110609011924/http://www.uefa.com/uefa/aboutuefa/organisation/executivecommittee/news/newsid%3D796145.html |archive-date=9 June 2011}}</ref> The stadium, which opened in 2005, was then the home stadium of both Bayern Munich and [[TSV 1860 Munich|1860 Munich]], and was used for six matches at the [[2006 FIFA World Cup]] including the opening match.

The stadium was hosting its first major European final. The [[Olympic Stadium (Munich)|Olympiastadion]] in Munich, the previous home of Bayern Munich and 1860 Munich, hosted three European Cup finals; in [[1979 European Cup final|1979]], [[1993 UEFA Champions League final|1993]] and [[1997 UEFA Champions League final|1997]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/newsid=1768453.html |title=Munich finals have habit for upsets |work=[[UEFA]] |publisher=Union of European Football Associations |date=1 March 2012|url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120321105822/http://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/newsid=1768453.html |archive-date=21 March 2012}}</ref> On each previous occasion, a European Cup final held in Munich had produced a first-time winner of the competition (Nottingham Forest, Olympique Marseille and Borussia Dortmund).<ref>{{cite web |title=Plays of the Day: Heroes in blue |url=http://en.espn.co.uk/football/sport/story/151555.html |work=ESPN |date=19 May 2012 |access-date=4 July 2012}}</ref>

During the match, the stadium was illuminated in green and turquoise to represent the official UEFA emblem of the Munich final, as the outer shell of the Allianz Arena can change colour.<ref>{{cite news |title=Allianz Arena gets a new colour |url=http://www.sueddeutsche.de/muenchen/champions-league-finale-in-muenchen-allianz-arena-bekommt-eine-neue-farbe-1.1344898|access-date=5 May 2012 |newspaper=[[Süddeutsche Zeitung]] |date=30 April 2012}}</ref>

==Background==
To reach the final, in the [[2011–12 UEFA Champions League knockout phase|knockout phase]] Bayern defeated [[FC Basel|Basel]], [[Olympique de Marseille|Marseille]], and [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] (3–1 on penalties after a 3–3 aggregate score),<ref>{{cite news |url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=340833&cc=5739 |title=Shootout woe for Madrid |date=25 April 2012 |publisher=ESPN Soccernet |access-date = 26 April 2012 |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20120428120359/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=340833&cc=5739 |archive-date = 28 April 2012 |url-status = dead |df=dmy-all}}</ref> while Chelsea overcame [[SSC Napoli|Napoli]],<ref>{{cite news |last1=McNulty |first1=Phil |title=Chelsea 4–1 Napoli aet (agg 5–4) |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/17282312 |access-date=25 August 2020 |work=BBC Sport |date=14 March 2012}}</ref> [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]],<ref>{{cite news |last1=Taylor |first1=Daniel |title=Chelsea's Frank Lampard sinks Benfica and sets up Barcelona semi-final |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2012/apr/04/chelsea-benfica-champions-league |access-date=25 August 2020 |work=The Guardian |date=4 April 2012}}</ref> and the defending champions [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] (3–2 on aggregate).<ref>{{cite news |last1=Dawkes |first1=Phil |title=Barcelona 2–2 Chelsea (agg 2–3) |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/17817584 |access-date=25 August 2020 |work=BBC Sport |date=24 April 2012}}</ref>

Both teams reached the final having already lost out in their domestic leagues (the [[2011–12 Bundesliga|Bundesliga]] and [[2011–12 Premier League|Premier League]] respectively), but having also reached the final of their domestic cup competitions (the [[2012 DFB-Pokal Final|DFB-Pokal]] and [[2012 FA Cup Final|FA Cup]] respectively), to be played prior to the Champions League final. Chelsea won the FA Cup by defeating Liverpool 2–1 thus were chasing a [[double (association football)|double]],<ref>{{cite news |title=Chelsea 2–1 Liverpool |first=Phil |last=McNulty |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/17878435 |work=BBC Sport |publisher=British Broadcasting Corporation |date=5 May 2012 |access-date=21 May 2012}}</ref> while Bayern lost the Final of the DFB-Pokal 5–2 to [[Borussia Dortmund]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Dortmund rout Bayern to claim double |url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story/_/id/1069150/borussia-dortmund-rout-bayern-munich-to-claim-historic-double?cc=5739 |work=ESPN Soccernet |publisher=ESPN |date=12 May 2012 |access-date=21 May 2012 |archive-date=16 May 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120516032245/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story/_/id/1069150/borussia-dortmund-rout-bayern-munich-to-claim-historic-double?cc=5739 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

Both clubs had lost their most recent Champions League final – Bayern in [[2010 UEFA Champions League final|2010]] to [[Inter Milan]] 2–0 and Chelsea in [[2008 UEFA Champions League final|2008]] in an all-English clash with [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] on penalties after a 1–1 draw. While that was Chelsea's only Champions League final, Bayern had previously played in eight Champions League/European Cup finals, winning four ([[1974 European Cup final|1974]], [[1975 European Cup final|1975]], [[1976 European Cup final|1976]], [[2001 UEFA Champions League final|2001]]) and losing four ([[1982 European Cup final|1982]], [[1987 European Cup final|1987]], [[1999 UEFA Champions League final|1999]] and 2010). The clubs had only met each other once in Europe before, with Chelsea winning 6–5 on aggregate in the quarter-finals of the [[2004–05 UEFA Champions League]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Bayern and Chelsea renew rivalry |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0254-0d7dd1d52131-ef15b8d04841-1000--bayern-and-chelsea-renew-rivalry/ |work=[[UEFA]] |publisher=Union of European Football Associations |date=26 April 2012}}</ref>

The match was the fourth occasion that a team had reached a final of the European Cup which was scheduled to be played at their own home ground, after [[1957 European Cup final|1957]], [[1965 European Cup final|1965]] and [[1984 European Cup final|1984]], and the first occasion since the tournament was rebranded to the UEFA Champions League. For this reason, fans of Bayern Munich called the match "Finale dahoam" ([[Bavarian language|Bavarian]] for "final at home"). This was the first time since [[2007 UEFA Champions League final|2007]] that neither of the participants were current champions of their domestic league. This was the sixth time that an English side and a German side had met in a European Cup/Champions League final; the other occasions were [[1975 European Cup final|1975]], [[1977 European Cup final|1977]], [[1980 European Cup final|1980]], [[1982 European Cup final|1982]] and [[1999 UEFA Champions League final|1999]]. It was also Bayern's fourth time facing an English side in the European Cup/Champions League final, having won in [[1975 European Cup final|1975 vs. Leeds United]] and lost in [[1982 European Cup final|1982 vs. Aston Villa]] and [[1999 UEFA Champions League final|1999 to Manchester United]].

==Pre-match==
===Ticketing===
The two teams each received 17,500 tickets to distribute to their supporters. A further 7,000 tickets were available for sale to fans worldwide via UEFA.com, with prices between €70 and €370. The remaining tickets were allocated to the local organising committee, UEFA's 53 national football associations, and commercial and broadcast partners.<ref>{{cite web |title=UEFA Champions League Final 2012 ticket sales launched |url=http://www.uefa.com/uefa/mediaservices/mediareleases/newsid=1761256.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120304004950/http://www.uefa.com/uefa/mediaservices/mediareleases/newsid=1761256.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=4 March 2012 |work=[[UEFA]] |publisher=Union of European Football Associations |date=29 February 2012}}</ref>

===Ambassador===
Former German player [[Paul Breitner]] was named as the ambassador for the final.<ref>{{cite web |title=Ambassador: Paul Breitner |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/01fb-0e137f75efda-229672f15958-1000--ambassador-paul-breitner/ |work=[[UEFA]] |publisher=Union of European Football Associations |date=1 March 2012 |access-date=19 May 2012}}</ref>

===Officials===
In May 2012, [[Pedro Proença]], the Portuguese [[referee (association football)|referee]] was selected to oversee the final.  Joining him, was fellow Portuguese officials Bertino Miranda and Ricardo Santos as [[assistant referee (association football)|assistant referees]], [[Jorge Sousa]] and [[Duarte Gomes]] as [[assistant referee (association football)#Additional assistant referee|additional assistant referees]], Tiago Trigo as [[assistant referee (association football)#Fifth official and reserve assistant referee|reserve assistant referee]], and Spaniard [[Carlos Velasco Carballo]] as [[assistant referee (association football)#Fourth official|fourth official]].<ref name="referee"/>

===Team selection===
[[File:DidiFinale12 (cropped).jpg|thumb|upright|[[Didier Drogba]] scored the equalising goal and the winning penalty.]]

Both clubs had players missing due to suspensions; Bayern were missing [[David Alaba]], [[Holger Badstuber]] and [[Luiz Gustavo]], while Chelsea were without [[Branislav Ivanović]], [[Raul Meireles]], [[Ramires]] and [[John Terry]].<ref>{{cite news |first=Matt |last=Zuvela |title=Bayern in Champions League final after Madrid thriller |url=http://www.dw.de/dw/article/0,,15910552,00.html |newspaper=[[Deutsche Welle]] |date=25 April 2012 |access-date=25 April 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |first=Florian |last=Haupt |title=Schock für Barcelona, Triumph und Tragödie für Chelsea |url=https://www.welt.de/sport/fussball/article106223466/Schock-fuer-Barcelona-Triumph-und-Tragoedie-fuer-Chelsea.html |language=de |newspaper=[[Die Welt]] |date=25 April 2012 |access-date=25 April 2012}}</ref> Terry was suspended after being [[Misconduct (association football)|sent off]] in the semi-final, which automatically excludes a player from the final. The other six all received [[Misconduct (association football)|yellow cards]] in the semi-finals, which took them over the limit of a third yellow card of the competition, which triggers an automatic suspension from the next match. Players union [[FIFPro]] appealed to UEFA to allow the players with yellow cards to play, seeing the punishment of "missing the match of your life" as too harsh; UEFA rejected the appeal and stated the rule would not be reviewed for at least three years.<ref>{{cite news |title=Uefa stands by yellow cards rules for Champions League |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/17924587 |work=BBC Sport |publisher=British Broadcasting Corporation |date=2 May 2012 |access-date=19 May 2012}}</ref> Ivanović stated how he "had no idea [he] was one booking away from missing the Champions League final."<ref>{{cite news |title=Ivanovic had no idea he could miss final |url=http://www.espn.co.uk/football/sport/story/148022.html|access-date=26 April 2012 |newspaper=[[ESPN (UK)|ESPN UK]] |date=26 April 2012|archive-date=10 August 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140810152323/http://www.espn.co.uk/football/sport/story/148022.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> UEFA confirmed that Chelsea captain Terry would be allowed to lift the trophy should Chelsea win, despite his suspension.<ref>{{cite news |title=John Terry can lift Champions League trophy if Chelsea win final |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/17860112 |work=BBC Sport |publisher=British Broadcasting Corporation |date=26 April 2012 |access-date=19 May 2012}}</ref> [[Ryan Bertrand]] also got his initial first-team start as a left winger ahead of his regular left back position.

Only two of the 36 players had previously been in a winning squad in a Champions League final: Chelsea's [[Paulo Ferreira]] and [[José Bosingwa]] were in the [[FC Porto|Porto]] squad in [[2004 UEFA Champions League final|2004]]. Ten of the Bayern 18 had earlier been in their squad that lost the [[2010 UEFA Champions League final|2010 final]], although only four started both games: [[Philipp Lahm]], [[Bastian Schweinsteiger]], [[Arjen Robben]] and [[Thomas Müller]]. Eight of the Chelsea squad had been in their losing [[2008 UEFA Champions League final|2008]] squad, including four who started both games: [[Petr Čech]], [[Ashley Cole]], [[Frank Lampard]] and [[Didier Drogba]].{{citation needed|date=June 2020}}

===Opening ceremony===
The [[UEFA Champions League Anthem]] was performed by German tenor [[Jonas Kaufmann]] and violinist [[David Garrett (musician)|David Garrett]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.david-garrett.com/2012/05/19/david-is-performing-at-the-champions-league-final/ |title=David Is Performing at the Champions League Final |date=19 May 2012 |website=David-Garrett.com |access-date=15 January 2020 |archive-date=22 June 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190622145101/https://www.david-garrett.com/2012/05/19/david-is-performing-at-the-champions-league-final/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Related events===
The UEFA Champions Festival was held at Munich's [[Olympiapark (Munich)|Olympiapark]] from 16 to 19 May.<ref>{{cite web |title=Olympiapark to stage UEFA Champions Festival |url=http://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/newsid=1788483.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120426235734/http://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/newsid=1788483.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=26 April 2012 |work=[[UEFA]] |publisher=Union of European Football Associations |date=24 April 2012}}</ref> An official public screening of the final took place at the Olympiastadion during the match,<ref>{{cite web |title=Official public screening of Champions League final |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/01fc-0e7e0734fb96-877b95fa94b1-1000--official-public-screening-of-champions-league-final/ |work=[[UEFA]] |publisher=Union of European Football Associations |date=27 April 2012}}</ref> with capacity for 65,000 fans, including a section for Chelsea supporters.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.sportingintelligence.com/2012/04/27/exclusive-uefa-to-sell-65000-new-munich-stadium-tickets-for-bayern-chelsea-270402/ |title=Uefa to sell 65,000 new Munich stadium tickets for Bayern-Chelsea |publisher=Sporting Intelligence |date=27 April 2012 |access-date=19 May 2012}}</ref> A second public screening was planned on the [[Theresienwiese]], where the famous [[Oktoberfest]] takes place.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.focus.de/sport/fussball/championsleague/champions-league-zweites-public-viewing-auf-theresienwiese-geplant_aid_747756.html |title=Second public screening planned on Theresienwiese |publisher=Focus Online |date=5 May 2012 }}{{Dead link|date=August 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref>

==Match==

===Summary===
[[File:G8 leaders watching football.jpg|thumb|British Prime Minister [[David Cameron]] and German Chancellor [[Angela Merkel]] watching the penalty shoot-out with US President [[Barack Obama]], French President [[François Hollande]], European Commission President [[José Manuel Barroso]] and others during the G8 summit.]]

Bayern had control for most of the match, with former Chelsea winger Robben having the best chance, which Čech deflected onto the frame of the goal with his legs. Chelsea, however, also had chances, with [[Salomon Kalou]] nearly finishing at the near post. Bayern kept pushing Chelsea to the limit but missed sitters from [[Mario Gómez]], who sent his shot over the bar; and Robben, who was blocked at the last second by [[Gary Cahill]]. Bayern took the lead in the 83rd minute, when [[Toni Kroos]] crossed in to Müller, who headed the ball down into the ground, causing it to bounce over Čech and in off the crossbar.<ref name=guard12>{{cite web |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2012/may/19/bayern-munich-chelsea-champions-league-final |title=Chelsea win Champions League on penalties over Bayern Munich |work=[[The Guardian]] |first=Daniel |last=Taylor |date=19 May 2012|access-date=19 December 2018}}</ref> Bayern took Müller off and replaced him with [[Daniel Van Buyten]] in an attempt to strengthen the defence. However, on 88 minutes, Chelsea won their first corner kick of the match, and when [[Juan Mata]] swung it in, Drogba got to it first and powered a header past [[Manuel Neuer]] at the near post for the equaliser. Chelsea won a free kick just outside the area in the 93rd minute, but Drogba smashed it over.

The game went to extra time, and Bayern had the first good chance of the extra 30 minutes when [[Ivica Olić]] inside the box passed to Gómez, but his shot was wide. Later, Drogba fouled [[Franck Ribéry]] in the penalty area, injuring him and earning Bayern a penalty; Robben took it, but his shot was saved by Čech.<ref name=guard12/> In the second half of extra time, Olić attempted to set up Van Buyten instead of taking a shot and the ball rolled wide of Čech's far post.{{citation needed|date=June 2020}}

[[File:Chelsea Champions League Winners 2012.jpg|thumb|left|Chelsea received the trophy from UEFA President [[Michel Platini]].]]

For the first time since 2008, when Chelsea had lost to Manchester United, the European Cup would be decided by penalties. Lahm went first and scored to Čech's left, as Čech got his fingertips to the ball but was unable to keep it out. Mata took Chelsea's first penalty, but his weak shot was saved by Neuer. Next was Gómez, who drilled his shot into the bottom-right corner. [[David Luiz]] took Chelsea's second penalty and scored with a powerful shot into the top corner after a long run up. Goalkeeper Neuer took Bayern's third penalty, and Čech went the right way again but was unable to keep his opposite number's low shot from creeping past him into the bottom-left corner. Lampard was next and he scored with a hard shot high and down the middle. Olić was next and taking his final competitive kick for Bayern, but Čech saved to his left. Cole then slotted his kick into the bottom-right corner just out of Neuer's reach to level the scores at 3–3 and hasten [[Sudden death (sport)#Association football|sudden death]]. Schweinsteiger, who had scored Bayern's decisive fifth penalty against Real Madrid's [[Iker Casillas]] in the semi-finals, was their fifth penalty taker again. However, Čech tipped his effort onto the post, having gone the correct direction for every Bayern penalty, to leave Chelsea one kick away from winning the trophy. In 2008, Drogba had missed out on taking Chelsea's fifth penalty against Manchester United, having been sent off in extra time; now in the same position, the Ivorian sent Neuer the wrong way and put his kick into the bottom-left corner to win it for Chelsea. It proved to be his final kick as a Chelsea player until his return in 2014.<ref name=guard12/>

The victory marked not only Chelsea's first ever European Cup, but also the first time a London team had won the competition – previously, aside from Chelsea's 2008 defeat to United, which was the last time an English club had won the competition until Liverpool’s triumph in the final against Tottenham in Madrid, 7 years later. [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] had also lost the 2006 final in Paris against Barcelona.<ref name=guard12/>

==Legends of Europe reunion match==

On 9 September 2023, the two clubs played a legends match at [[Stamford Bridge (stadium)|Stamford Bridge]] to benefit The Chelsea Foundation and The Royal Marsden Cancer Charity. The match was also in memory of former Chelsea and Italy player [[Gianluca Vialli]], who had died at the Royal Marsden Hospital on 6 January of pancreatic cancer at the age of 58.

Chelsea included most of their team from the 2012 final and also included captain Terry and Ramires, who had both missed the final due to suspension, and [[Michael Essien]], who was an unused substitute in 2012. [[Gianfranco Zola]], [[Jody Morris]] and [[Salomon Kalou]] were among the players who returned, and Di Matteo also returned to manage the side. Bayern Munich included only Van Buyten from their 2012 team but included a number of their players from their [[2001 UEFA Champions League final|2001]] team that had beaten Valencia in Milan, including [[Owen Hargreaves]], [[Giovane Elber]] and [[Thomas Linke]]. 2001 captain [[Stefan Effenberg]] also co-managed alongside [[Raimond Aumann]]. Chelsea won 4–0 with goals from Essien, Terry, Cahill and [[Tiago Mendes]].<ref>{{cite web |author=Chelsea Football Club |title=Chelsea Legends 4–0 FC Bayern – Legends of Europe – 09/09/2023 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=60NSCKwZj-c |website=YouTube |access-date=14 September 2023 |date=9 September 2023 |language=en}}</ref>
